blocks.title: Maths · introduce order of operations
blocks.notes: Introduce the agreed order for whole-number expressions. An expression is a calculation written with numbers and operation signs. Model 6 + 4 × 3 = 6 + 12 = 18, then (6 + 4) × 3 = 10 × 3 = 30. Brackets change which calculation happens first. Work inside brackets first, then multiplication and division from left to right, then addition and subtraction from left to right. Multiplication is not always before division. Practise 8 + 2 × 5 = 18, (8 + 2) × 5 = 50 and 18 ÷ 3 × 2 = 12, recording one step per line and explaining the first step. Check independently with 24 ÷ (2 + 4) × 3 = 24 ÷ 6 × 3 = 4 × 3 = 12. The existing Math Antics Order of Operations lesson is optional explanation support; the board model and paper practice provide the complete non-video route. Keep exponents for a later lesson or optional extension, not this introduction.
blocks.firstAction: Get paper and a pencil ready. Which operation comes first in 6 + 4 × 3?
studentSteps: Compare 6 + 4 × 3 with (6 + 4) × 3. Explain what the brackets change.
Try 8 + 2 × 5, (8 + 2) × 5 and 18 ÷ 3 × 2. Show one step per line.
Work inside brackets first; then × and ÷ from left to right; then + and − from left to right.
On your own, solve 24 ÷ (2 + 4) × 3. Explain your first step and check your calculation.
blocks.firstActionKo: 종이와 연필을 준비하세요. 6 + 4 × 3에서 무엇을 먼저 계산할까요?
